feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The geometry is the iteration 5 set, which is the best-supported layout: iteration 4 (+/-0.03, 0.016 footprint) scored 52.198 and iteration 5 (+/-0.036) scored 52.356, with slalom line loss at 1 and slalom progress near 0.11 in both. Widening the outer pair from 0.03 to 0.036 changed slalom rms_error only from 0.0302 to 0.0303, so the outer reach is not clearly the binding limit. Iteration 2 showed that the lighter body (0.14 m, 0.6 kg) cut s-bend progress to 0.1275, so the baseline body stays. Iteration 0 (kp 2.0, base 1.6) had oscillation 0.158 on the slalom, much like the kp 2.5 runs, which suggests the oscillation is not set by kp alone. This race changes the controller only (kd 0.15 to 0.25), so the geometry is being measured against a fixed platform. Next race: if slalom line loss clears, the sensing layout is sufficient and the next lever is small (keep the geometry). If line loss stays at 1 and oscillation is unchanged, the controller is no longer the limit and wheel_track is the remaining geometry lever. If rms_error rises, the body and sensors are not the cause, and the next move is to reduce the sensor reach rather than widen it.
requested_changes: If slalom line_loss_events stays at 1 with progress near 0.11 after the kd change: test wheel_track 0.14 (from 0.12), changing nothing else. Evidence: iterations 3 to 5 changed sensing and body and never changed the turn rate per wheel, and the slalom line loss has stayed at 1 across all of them.

If slalom line_loss_events clears to 0 with rms_error at or below 0.031: keep sensor_positions at x = +/-0.036, y = 0.04, sensor_size 0.016, and the 0.18 m, 0.8 kg body. Evidence: iteration 5 is the best-supported set (score 52.356), and iteration 4 vs 3 showed the 0.016 footprint was neutral to slightly positive.
Do not change body_length or mass again. Evidence: iteration 2 (0.14 m, 0.6 kg) cut s-bend progress from 0.16 to 0.1275, and iteration 3 recovered it to 0.16 on the baseline body.
